body_text:
The rational order is dense: whenever $p<q$ in $\mathbb{Q}$, the
midpoint $(p+q)/2$ is rational and satisfies $p<(p+q)/2<q$. The
rationals are also dense in the reals, but they are not complete;
for example, the rational numbers whose square is less than $2$
have no least upper bound in $\mathbb{Q}$.
